recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how many terms the A.P. has and how you get the common difference.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the terms and find the common difference
steps.margin_note: First mark. The examiner wants the term count stated: five means give seven terms, so 26 is the 7th term and equals a + 6d.
steps.memory_tip: Two ends plus five means make seven terms, so the gap is counted six times.
lines: Inserting five arithmetic means between 8 and 26 gives 7 terms in A.P.
Here a = 8 and the 7th term is 26

recall.must_convey: That five means make seven terms, so 8 + 6d = 26 and d = 3.
accept: five means between two numbers make seven terms
twenty six is the seventh term so eight plus six d equals twenty six
the common difference comes out as three
aidu means unte seven terms, so d equals three vasthundi
find d from the seventh term

steps.why: The five means sit between the two given numbers, so the A.P. has 5 + 2 = 7 terms. Once 26 is named as the 7th term, the one unknown d comes out of a single equation.
common_mistakes: Taking 26 as the 5th term instead of the 7th.
Writing a + 5d = 26, which counts only the means and leaves out one gap.

steps.label: Write the five means
steps.margin_note: Second mark. All five values must be listed. Ending at 23 and seeing that 23 + 3 = 26 is the check the examiner expects you to have made.
steps.memory_tip: Keep adding 3 to 8 until you reach 26; the numbers you pass on the way are the means.
lines: The means are the 2nd to the 6th terms, got by adding d = 3 each time:

recall.must_convey: That adding 3 repeatedly from 8 gives the means 11, 14, 17, 20, 23.
accept: add three each time starting from eight
eleven fourteen seventeen twenty and twenty three
the means are the second to the sixth terms
moodu add chesukuntu vellali, eleven fourteen seventeen twenty twenty three
check that twenty three plus three is twenty six

steps.why: Adding d repeatedly is quicker than working out a + nd five separate times, and the check costs nothing: one more 3 after 23 lands exactly on 26.
common_mistakes: Listing 8 and 26 among the means, which gives seven values instead of five.
Stopping after four means because the counting was started at 8.
